interpretations.rationale: The question is answered by a completed, admitted execution. Receipt 037218ff747d43cfa5af7925dccf6d2d ran decided_suffix_collapses_trimmed_prefix (exit 0, test passed) and all three comparisons are complete: from=1 returns len 3 (holds, evaluated event 1), from=4 returns len 2 (holds, evaluated event 2), and the cursor replay reports duplicates true (holds, evaluated event 3). Event 0 confirms the setup, with node 1 leader in Accept, both nodes decided 6 and compacted 4. The events show that read_decided_suffix(1) returns one Trimmed(4) element in place of the four trimmed indices plus Decided(5) and Decided(6), so the vector has 3 elements while decided-minus-from is 5; the runtime's only per-subscriber state is next_idx, incremented once per delivered element, so a catch-up starting below the compacted index ends at 4 instead of 6, and the next push reads from 4 and delivers entries 5 and 6 a second time (delivered_values 5,6,5,6, duplicate_values 5,6) with no new decision in between. subscribe_decided accepts any from, does not reject a compacted start, and does not advance the cursor to decided after a collapsed catch-up; the same boundary is crossed by a subscriber whose cursor lags behind compaction. interpretations.rationale: The pending completion path can report a false success, under a schedule the actor does not exclude. A pending append_notify keeps only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot). drain_notifiers evaluates, in order, Ok when assigned_idx <= decided, then Superseded when the assignment ballot is below the current promise ballot, then Timeout; the Ok arm reads no log entry and never checks that the value at assigned_idx is the caller's entry. The origin can hold an assignment made when it was leader or when a leader accepted its proposal, lose leadership to a higher ballot, and then have its own decided index advance past assigned_idx with a different value at that index: the runtime's own Superseded regression test constructs exactly that replacement (the old leader accepts locally with its outgoing cut, a new leader appends a fresh entry that decides at the same index, and the origin learns of the new ballot). Whether the pending resolves Ok or Superseded then depends only on whether a drain runs after the promise advanced but before decided reached assigned_idx. drain_notifiers runs only in the actor's tick branch; handling an incoming message never drains. Nothing orders a tick between the ballot change and the decided advance, so when the origin processes the higher-ballot Prepare and then the message that carries decided >= assigned_idx within one tick interval, the Ok arm wins and the caller is told its entry is decided at an index that holds a different entry. With a legal user-set tick_period that exceeds the leadership-turnover interval, that ordering is deterministic; with a short period it is a race. The gap on the reachable schedule is therefore answered on source grounds: no mechanism prevents it, and a legal configuration makes it the expected ordering.

3f84facd1a81451882518e32ee8be535-gap-0.explanation: Reachable. drain_notifiers is invoked only from the tick branch (actor.rs tick handling), while handle_incoming_tracked processes messages without draining; the actor polls the tick first each iteration but the tick fires at most once per configured period. The ballot change (Prepare/AcceptSync from the new leader) and the decided advance (AcceptDecide/Decide from that leader) are separate messages that can both be processed inside one period. If the period exceeds the turnover interval, the pending sees decided >= assigned_idx and a stale assignment ballot at the same drain, and the Ok arm precedes the Superseded arm. Since tick_period is user-set and only advised to match the ServerConfig tick budget, this ordering is legal and deterministic in that configuration.

counterevidence: The Superseded regression test observes Superseded for the same replacement scenario, which shows the other ordering is common in its configuration; that is evidence about that schedule, not a mechanism that guarantees it.
When the new leader adopts the caller's value at assigned_idx, Ok is accurate and returning it must not be suppressed; the defect is limited to the replaced-value case.
The Superseded doc already calls the error a heuristic and tells callers to inspect the index, which mitigates the Superseded path but not a false Ok.
limitations: No execution of the runtime crate is possible from the omnipaxos harness (omnipaxos_runtime is not a dev-dependency), so the schedule is established by source reasoning plus the runtime's own saved test expectations, not by a measured actor run.
The false Ok needs the caller's entry to have been accepted without a majority and then replaced at the same index; if the entry is adopted by the new leader, Ok is correct.
The exact duration of an in-process leadership turnover relative to a given tick_period is unmeasured here.

interpretations.rationale: The source establishes the mechanism: a pending append_notify stores only (assigned_idx, assignment_ballot), and drain_notifiers resolves Ok whenever decided_idx >= assigned_idx before it checks whether that ballot has been superseded; nothing in the Ok path reads the entry at assigned_idx. The runtime's own tests establish both premises the false Ok would need: Ok(idx) is expected to mean the caller's value is decided at idx, and an entry accepted only on the old leader can be replaced at the same index by a different decided value while the origin learns of the new ballot. What is not yet established is the decisive schedule: the origin's actor drains on each tick (10 ms by default) and when commands arrive, so a drain while decided_idx < assigned_idx and the promise ballot has already changed yields Superseded and avoids the false Ok. A false Ok requires the decided advance to assigned_idx and the ballot change to be visible in the same drain pass, or the decided advance to arrive with the new ballot before any intervening tick. The runtime crate is not a dev-dependency of the omnipaxos test target, so the fixed assurance_generated harness cannot execute this path; the open question is therefore the actor-level interleaving and log-content identity, not the core Paxos decision rule.
counterevidence: The Superseded doc explicitly calls itself a heuristic and notes the entry can still be decided under the new ballot at log_entry_idx; when the caller's entry survives reconciliation, returning Ok once decided_idx reaches idx is correct and must not be suppressed.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading gives a concrete mechanism. In InternalStorage::read, when from is below the compacted index the result is one create_compacted_entry element followed by one element per entry from compacted_idx to the requested end, so for from < compacted_idx the vector has fewer elements than decided_idx - from; the Trimmed(t)/Snapshotted variant is a marker for the whole trimmed prefix, not one index. The runtime stores only next_idx per subscriber, increments it once per element pushed (push_to_sub and push_to_all_subs), and push_to_all_subs computes start = sub.next_idx - min_next assuming one element per index. A subscription or catch-up at from < compacted therefore ends with next_idx = from + 1 + (decided - compacted), short of decided, and the next push re-reads from that cursor and re-sends entries after the compacted index. subscribe_decided accepts any from and documents a single in-order stream; nothing rejects or compensates for a compacted starting index. The retained execution is needed to pin the core's returned shape (element count and kinds) and the resulting replay; the claim remains unresolved until that receipt is associated.
counterevidence: If the caller only ever subscribes at or above the compacted index, read_decided_suffix returns exactly one element per index and the cursor arithmetic is aligned; the defect is limited to a starting or lagging cursor below compaction.
A Trimmed/Snapshotted marker is a documented LogEntry variant, so delivering it is not itself wrong; the defect is the cursor advance that treats the marker as one index.
